# PEAK Game Wiki: Full Machine-Readable Site Context

> PEAK Game Wiki is an independent, multilingual reference for the Steam co-op climbing game PEAK. It connects map rotation, biomes, equipment, badges, Steam achievements, co-op play, troubleshooting, and official update context. It is a fan reference, not a developer or publisher site, and it does not host the game or provide a direct download.

## 1. Identity and Audience

- Canonical identity: PEAK Game Wiki at https://peak-game.wiki/
- Audience: PEAK players checking a route before a climb, comparing item roles, understanding progress systems, solving multiplayer problems, or reviewing changes after an update.
- Format: Static HTML pages generated from repository source and published as a Cloudflare Pages site.
- Languages: English, Simplified Chinese, Spanish, Japanese, French, German, Portuguese, Korean, and Italian. English is the default machine-readable resource language.
- Independence: The site does not claim affiliation with Landfall, the PEAK developers, Steam, or any external wiki. Official links are labeled as official; practical recommendations are editorial field notes.

## 2. Content Structure

### Homepage - https://peak-game.wiki/

The homepage combines a build-time daily-map entry point, a version desk, a searchable item database, badge and achievement context, co-op field notes, FAQ answers, and source links. It currently presents a 134-item reference scope and labels the homepage update snapshot as Patch 2.6.b checked on 6 October 2026. Map and patch details remain version-sensitive.

### Map today and rotation - https://peak-game.wiki/map-rotation

This page answers the time-sensitive map query with the dated build-time map panel and explains how to confirm the active route in-game. It separates a community or build-time estimate from an official announcement, distinguishes maps, routes, and biomes, and gives a practical checklist for route scouting, shared utility, recovery, and version notes.

### Items list - https://peak-game.wiki/items/

The item catalog is a searchable list of 134 entries grouped around gear, food, and utility. Individual entries include maintained names and concise role or source notes. The catalog is not a guarantee of every effect, drop location, value, or current behavior; check the game and official updates when a patch could change an item.

### Achievements guide - https://peak-game.wiki/achievements

The achievements guide treats Steam achievements as platform progress and in-game badges as a separate system. It explains how to build a version-aware checklist, record route, mode, team, evidence, and date, and recheck custom runs or missing unlocks against the current game and official Steam page.

### Badges guide - https://peak-game.wiki/badges-guide/

The badges guide organizes in-game badge groups, route context, unlock notes, and source boundaries. It is intended for progress planning and does not turn an unverified community condition into a permanent rule.

### Contact and policy pages

- Contact: https://peak-game.wiki/contact/ - Send source-backed corrections, outdated map reports, copyright concerns, or site suggestions.
- About: https://peak-game.wiki/about - Project purpose, source policy, and independence statement.
- Privacy: https://peak-game.wiki/privacy - Cloudflare delivery, analytics, advertising, cookies, and third-party-link disclosures.
- Terms: https://peak-game.wiki/terms - Fan-site disclaimer, accuracy limits, external sources, and acceptable use.

## 4. FAQ and Common Questions

### Is PEAK single player?

The site reports that PEAK can be played solo or cooperatively, while the official Steam page is the authority for the current modes and group-size statement.

### How many players can join a PEAK game?

The homepage currently describes an official Steam group size of up to four players. Confirm the current store and patch information before organizing a session.

### How does the PEAK daily map work?

Use the dated panel at the top of the map rotation page as a build-time planning entry, then confirm the active route in the current game. The site does not present an unverified fixed sequence as a live official result.

### Where are the latest PEAK patch notes?

Use the homepage update desk and the PEAK game update timeline for the maintained index, then open the official Steam news feed for exact implementation details. The homepage snapshot currently identifies Patch 2.6.b as checked on 6 October 2026.

### Are PEAK badges and Steam achievements the same?

No. Steam achievements are platform progress; in-game badges are a separate game progress surface. The site keeps them in separate sections and recommends tracking exact names, actions, modes, and evidence separately.

### Why is a map, item, or achievement answer marked pending?

Pending means the current repository sources do not verify the claim strongly enough for a definitive statement. The editor leaves the gap visible and points to the current game or official source rather than filling it by inference.

## 5. Sources and Fact Boundaries

### Official facts

Use the official PEAK Steam store for current platform, mode, group-size, and first-party media statements: https://store.steampowered.com/app/3527290/PEAK/. Use the official Steam news feed for update titles, dates, and exact patch wording: https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/3527290.

### Maintained site data

The build reads repository data such as `data/today-map.json`, `data/peak-map-history.json`, and `data/peak-updates.json`. These support dated snapshots and history tables, but a build-time record is not automatically an official announcement or a guarantee of a future route.

### Editorial guidance

Route planning, loadout suggestions, troubleshooting order, and co-op checklists are editorial guidance. They are useful decision aids but should not be quoted as official developer rules unless the page links a first-party source for that specific claim.

### Community material

Community-maintained item or map references may be credited on the relevant page. They are not silently upgraded to official facts. The cooking page, for example, distinguishes community item notes from official patch context.

## 6. Time-Sensitive Information

- Daily map panels and rotation history are tied to a build date and may become stale after a reset, map-pool change, or patch.
- Patch titles and update summaries are dated snapshots; the official Steam post remains the authority for full mechanics.
- Prices, platforms, item effects, achievement conditions, multiplayer behavior, and save behavior can change with releases or regional settings.
- When a source cannot be checked, the site uses pending or cautious language. It does not infer a price, feature, platform, download, fixed route, or unsupported product conclusion.
- Last reviewed for this resource: 2026-10-08.

## 7. Multilingual Entry Points

The generated site preserves the existing locale paths and hreflang links: English `/`, Chinese `/zh/`, Spanish `/es/`, Japanese `/ja/`, French `/fr/`, German `/de/`, Portuguese `/pt/`, Korean `/ko/`, and Italian `/it/`. Each localized page uses its locale route for internal links. The machine-readable files remain at the root so assistants have one stable default source.
